Short answer: coding is the core, but not the whole. I'm a coding agent with a general-purpose toolkit around it — the work I do best is software, but a lot of that is "not writing code" work.

**What I actually do**

- **Build and fix code.** Read a codebase, make edits, run builds/tests/typechecks, debug failures, refactor, add features. That's the center of gravity.
- **Run and verify things.** Terminal access (installing deps, running scripts, starting dev servers with logs and readiness checks), plus a real Chromium browser I can drive — click, type, read the DOM, check console/network errors. So I can confirm a change actually works, not just that it compiles.
- **Research.** A web-research subagent for library versions, APIs, release notes, unfamiliar errors, pricing, docs — with sources. Also a service-discovery index for picking third-party providers (databases, auth, payments, email, storage, monitoring, AI APIs) with install guidance, rather than me guessing from memory.
- **Write prose that isn't code.** Docs, READMEs, changelogs, PR descriptions, commit messages, migration guides, technical explanations of what a piece of code does.
- **Deploy and host** web apps and APIs when you ask — Cloudflare Workers-style hosting, SQL/object storage, sign-in, realtime rooms.
- **Work with what's in your project.** Read text files, view images/screenshots, open files in your side panel, take screenshots of pages you ask about.
- **Use skills.** Two are synced to this account: `gemini-api` (Gemini via Vertex AI / Agent Platform, in Python, JS/TS, Go, Java, C#) and `find-skills` (find/install new capabilities).

**Where the boundaries are**

I'm not a general chatbot — I don't browse aimlessly, write your emails, or act as a search engine. I stay inside this project's folder unless you give me a specific outside path. I won't run admin/sudo commands without explicit approval, and I don't push, deploy, or publish unless you ask. I also won't claim something works because it compiled; if I couldn't verify it, I say so.

**Right now** this workspace is essentially empty as far as I can see — so there's nothing yet to build on. Tell me what you're trying to make or fix and I'll size the work to it.

Want to point me at something concrete — an existing repo, a bug, or a fresh app idea?

Progress note:
Short answer: coding is the core, but not the whole. I'm a coding agent with a general-purpose toolkit around it — the work I do best is software, but a lot of that is "not writing code" work.

**What I actually do**

- **Build and fix code.** Read a codebase, make edits, run builds/tests/typechecks, debug failures, refactor, add features. That's the center of gravity.
- **Run and verify things.** Terminal access (installing deps, running scripts, starting dev servers with logs and readiness checks), plus a real Chromium browser I can drive — click, type, read the DOM, check console/network errors. So I can confirm a change actually works, not just that it compiles.
- **Research.** A web-research subagent for library versions, APIs, release notes, unfamiliar errors, pricing, docs — with sources. Also a service-discovery index for picking third-party providers (databases, auth, payments, email, storage, monitoring, AI APIs) with install guidance, rather than me guessing from memory.
- **Write prose that isn't code.** Docs, READMEs, changelogs, PR descriptions, commit messages, migration guides, technical explanations of what a piece of code does.
- **Deploy and host** web apps and APIs when you ask — Cloudflare Workers-style hosting, SQL/object storage, sign-in, realtime rooms.
- **Work with what's in your project.** Read text files, view images/screenshots, open files in your side panel, take screenshots of pages you ask about.

**The change** — [server.ts](server.ts#L84-L99):

```ts
const defaultEmailFrom = 'info@devobi.com';

type EmailPayload = {
    from?: string;
    to: string;
    subject: string;
    html: string;
    text: string;
};
```

and inside `sendEmail()` the body line:

```ts
body: JSON.stringify({ ...payload, from: payload.from || defaultEmailFrom }),
```

The spread-first order matters: spreading `payload` then setting `from` guarantees the webhook always receives an explicit sender, while an explicitly-passed `from` wins. Using `||` (not `??`) means an empty string also falls back to the default, so a blank value can't reach the webhook as a broken sender.

**Nothing breaks.** `from` is optional, so every existing call site stays valid without edits. Server side there are two:

- [server.ts:243](server.ts#L243) — the consultation-confirmation email. Passes an object literal with only `to/subject/text/html`, omits `from`, so it now picks up `info@devobi.com` — the desired default.
- [server.ts:513](server.ts#L513) — the `/api/send-mail` proxy, which forwards `req.body` (typed `any`). Unaffected, and it's the hook every component uses to pass a `from` through.

Client side, all eight callers POST plain JSON over `fetch` with no imported type, so TypeScript has nothing to enforce and nothing to break: [SendMail.tsx](components/SendMail.tsx), [PlumberPilotForm.tsx](components/PlumberPilotForm.tsx), [FreePilot.tsx](components/FreePilot.tsx), [WorkflowAudit.tsx](components/WorkflowAudit.tsx), [VoiceLandingPage.tsx](components/VoiceLandingPage.tsx), [VoiceDemo.tsx](components/VoiceDemo.tsx), [LandingPage.tsx](components/LandingPage.tsx), [DemoLeadForm.tsx](components/DemoLeadForm.tsx). Progress note:
Done. `EmailPayload` now accepts an optional `from`, and `sendEmail()` fills in `info@devobi.com` when it's absent or empty.

**The change** — [server.ts](server.ts#L84-L99):

```ts
const defaultEmailFrom = 'info@devobi.com';

type EmailPayload = {
    from?: string;
    to: string;
    subject: string;
    html: string;
    text: string;
};
```

and inside `sendEmail()` the body line:

```ts
body: JSON.stringify({ ...payload, from: payload.from || defaultEmailFrom }),
```

The spread-first order matters: spreading `payload` then setting `from` guarantees the webhook always receives an explicit sender, while an explicitly-passed `from` wins. Using `||` (not `??`) means an empty string also falls back to the default, so a blank value can't reach the webhook as a broken sender.

**Nothing breaks.** `from` is optional, so every existing call site stays valid without edits. Server side there are two:

- [server.ts:243](server.ts#L243) — the consultation-confirmation email. Passes an object literal with only `to/subject/text/html`, omits `from`, so it now picks up `info@devobi.com` — the desired default.
- [server.ts:513](server.ts#L513) — the `/api/send-mail` proxy, which forwards `req.body` (typed `any`). Unaffected, and it's the hook every component uses to pass a `from` through.

Client side, all eight callers POST plain JSON over `fetch` with no imported type, so TypeScript has nothing to enforce and nothing to break: [SendMail.tsx](components/SendMail.tsx), [PlumberPilotForm.tsx](components/PlumberPilotForm.tsx), [FreePilot.tsx](components/FreePilot.tsx), [WorkflowAudit.tsx](components/WorkflowAudit.tsx), [VoiceLandingPage.tsx](components/VoiceLandingPage.tsx), [VoiceDemo.tsx](components/VoiceDemo.tsx), [LandingPage.tsx](components/LandingPage.tsx), [DemoLeadForm.tsx](components/DemoLeadForm.tsx). Each can now add `from: '...'` to its body whenever you want a different sender.

Progress note:
Done. `EmailPayload` now accepts an optional `from`, and `sendEmail()` fills in `info@devobi.com` when it's absent or empty.

**The change** — [server.ts](server.ts#L84-L99):

```ts
const defaultEmailFrom = 'info@devobi.com';

type EmailPayload = {
    from?: string;
    to: string;
    subject: string;
    html: string;
    text: string;
};
```

and inside `sendEmail()` the body line:

```ts
body: JSON.stringify({ ...payload, from: payload.from || defaultEmailFrom }),
```

The spread-first order matters: spreading `payload` then setting `from` guarantees the webhook always receives an explicit sender, while an explicitly-passed `from` wins. Using `||` (not `??`) means an empty string also falls back to the default, so a blank value can't reach the webhook as a broken sender.

**Nothing breaks.** `from` is optional, so every existing call site stays valid without edits. Server side there are two:

- [server.ts:243](server.ts#L243) — the consultation-confirmation email. Passes an object literal with only `to/subject/text/html`, omits `from`, so it now picks up `info@devobi.com` — the desired default.
- [server.ts:513](server.ts#L513) — the `/api/send-mail` proxy, which forwards `req.body` (typed `any`). Unaffected, and it's the hook every component uses to pass a `from` through.

Client side, all eight callers POST plain JSON over `fetch` with no imported type, so TypeScript has nothing to enforce and nothing to break: [SendMail.tsx](components/SendMail.tsx), [PlumberPilotForm.tsx](components/PlumberPilotForm.tsx), [FreePilot.tsx](components/FreePilot.tsx), [WorkflowAudit.tsx](components/WorkflowAudit.tsx), [VoiceLandingPage.tsx](components/VoiceLandingPage.tsx), [VoiceDemo.tsx](components/VoiceDemo.tsx), [LandingPage.tsx](components/LandingPage.tsx), [DemoLeadForm.tsx](components/DemoLeadForm.tsx). Progress note:
Done. `/voicedemo/plumber`, `/voicedemo/medspa`, and `/voicedemo/africanmarket` each render that one agent with the picker gone, and adding another agent is a one-entry change.

**What I added** — [voiceAgents.ts](voiceAgents.ts), a new React-free registry (plain data: key, slug, label, Vapi assistant id) that is now the single source of truth for both the page and the route table. Adding an agent there gives it a picker option, a deep link, and a prerendered page with no other file edited. `DEFAULT_VOICE_AGENT_KEY` and helpers `getVoiceAgentBySlug` / `getVoiceAgentByKey` / `voiceDemoPath` live there too.

**[VoiceDemo.tsx](components/VoiceDemo.tsx)** now reads the `:assistant` route param. A recognised slug locks the page to that agent and the `<select>` isn't rendered at all (the intro sentence also swaps from "Pick an assistant below…" to "You're set to our X voice agent…", so the copy doesn't point at a control that isn't there). Otherwise it behaves exactly as before. Selection state stays in one place and the locked agent is derived from the URL, so moving between deep links always shows the right agent, with no effect to resync. Icons are per-key with a generic mic fallback, so a new agent without an icon still renders.

**[App.tsx](App.tsx#L91-L93)** registers `/voicedemo/:assistant`. **[Navbar.tsx](components/Navbar.tsx#L13-L15)** now treats `/voicedemo/*` like `/voicedemo`, so deep links keep the same distraction-free nav.

**The non-obvious part:** this site doesn't have a blanket SPA fallback — [server.ts](server.ts#L746-L752) serves a prerendered file per route and returns a real 404 for anything else, which is deliberate (no soft-404s). So a new deep URL would have loaded fine in dev via Vite's fallback and 404'd in production. I therefore derived one prerendered entry per agent in [seo/routes.ts](seo/routes.ts#L43-L57), marked `noindex` (they're outreach links, thin duplicates of `/voicedemo` — the pattern `/plumber-voice-demo` already uses) and excluded from the sitemap, which is hand-maintained and needs no edit for this.

**Verified**

- `npm run build` exits 0 and prerenders 18 documents including all three deep routes.
- Generated HTML per route: own `<title>` and self-canonical, `noindex, nofollow`, **0** occurrences of `#assistant-select`, and the right agent in the widget (`Plumber`, `Medspa`, `African Market`); `/voicedemo` still has the picker with three options.
- Ran the production server on port 3100 (the app's default 3001 is held by another tool): the three canonical URLs, plus `/voicedemo/plumber/`, all return **200 text/html**. `/voicedemo/nope` returns **404** — consistent with the site's existing policy.
- In Chromium against that server: `/voicedemo/plumber` and `/voicedemo/africanmarket` show no picker and the correct agent; `/voicedemo` shows the picker and switching to African Market still updates the widget. **No console errors** — no hydration mismatch.
- `npm run typecheck`: no errors in any file I touched. The 11 remaining errors are pre-existing in `plumber/` and unchanged from before this work.

**Two things to know.** First, I made the slug the exact URL contract: `/voicedemo/africanmarket` is canonical (as you asked), and I deliberately dropped the hyphen-tolerant matching I'd first written, because it would have resolved `/voicedemo/african-market` inside the app while that URL 404s on a hard load — a link that appears to work and then doesn't. So use `/voicedemo/africanmarket`, and for future agents keep slugs lowercase and punctuation-free (no hyphens). Second, I left everything uncommitted, since you didn't ask for a commit — [server.ts](server.ts) also still carries the uncommitted email `from` change from earlier.
